description:
FILED s473t6d (Opus, 2026-09-20), found by #1954's breaking-case probe
(`probes/p7.pl` row 17); PRE-EXISTING (identical on a `268d7e00` extraction).

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL):

    sub mk { return [1,2] }
    for (mk()) { print "ref=", ref($_), "\n" }

    perl: ref=ARRAY          (ONE iteration -- a sub returning one scalar)
    PCL:  ref=                (two iterations, $_ = 1 then 2)

MECHANISM: the #267 rule (a foreach list of single SCALAR operands emits
`(vector ...)` rather than going through `%p-flatten-for-list`) is decided
from the SIGIL, which is compile-time knowledge.  A sub call has no sigil:
`mk()` may return a list or one scalar, and at runtime a box wrapping a vector
is indistinguishable from an @array box -- the very ambiguity
`_foreach_single_scalar_p`'s comment records.  So this is NOT another arm in
that predicate; it needs the runtime to be able to tell a REFERENCE box from
an @array box, which is the `ref-kind` slot that was measured and REJECTED
(ruled s335).

WHAT WOULD DECIDE IT: `p-sub` already knows the call's CONTEXT.  A sub called
in the foreach list is called in LIST context, and what it returns is a LIST
of values; the loss is that a single returned REFERENCE is then spread.  The
honest shapes to measure before designing anything:

    sub one  { return [1,2] }            # one ref      -> 1 iteration
    sub many { return ([1],[2]) }        # two refs     -> 2 iterations
    sub arr  { my @a=(1,2); return @a }  # a real list  -> 2 iterations

`many` and `arr` already work; only `one` is wrong, and the three are
indistinguishable to the flattener.  The fix therefore lives in how a sub's
return VALUE carries its ref-ness -- the same question #1991 and #551 ask from
their own sides.

ROWS: no blessed row is behind it today (found by probe), but the shape is
everyday Perl (`for (get_config()) {...}`) and it is SILENT.

=== s543c (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-21, CODE 64353611) ===
VERDICT: LIVE -- as filed, ordinary code (silent):
    sub mk { return [1,2] } for (mk()) { print "ref=", ref($_), "\n" }
    perl: ref=ARRAY (one iteration)      PCL: ref= / ref= (two iterations over the referent)
  The same for a hash ref (`sub hr { {a=>1} }` -> 2 iterations of nothing) and an implicit-tail array ref (`sub tail { [3,4] }`);
  `many` (two refs) and `arr` (a real list) = perl.
LABEL: silent (already in the subject).

=== DONE (s543e, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-21) ===
MEASURED -- the task's suspect is NOT the mechanism: `for (mk())` emits `(p-foreach ($_ (p-list-ctx (pl-mk))) ...)`, not #267's `(vector ...)`.  The list form's value in list context is the sub's single return value, a BOX holding the vector, and %p-flatten-for-list had an arm "p-box wrapping a vector (@array passed directly) -> iterate over elements" (and its hash arm unboxed first, so a hash ref spread into pairs).  Instrumented (a stderr marker in both arms, 60 foreach-heavy Pl/t files run): NO gate foreach list reached the box arm -- an aggregate VALUE is never boxed (p-scalar's invariant; arrays are raw adjustable vectors, lists raw vectors) -- while every call / method call / `&$c()` / `$c->()` / `scalar(...)` / `do {}` / ternary arm returning ONE reference did.  The s335 ruling (no ref-kind slot) stands: none is needed.
FIX (cl/ only; emission unchanged): %p-flatten-for-list takes a BOX as ONE element, tested BEFORE the unbox (a tied scalar is no longer FETCHed to build the list; the loop variable aliases it).  The comments in Pl/Parser.pm `_foreach_single_scalar_p` and Pl/Parser2.pm that described the runtime ambiguity are updated (#267's rule stays as the statically-sized emission).
PROBES: scratch/s543e/p6/for.pl (30 rows: the task's + `for (mk(), mk())`, `for (mk(), 1)`, `for my $x (mk())`, `for (@{ mk() })` (control), method calls in both shapes, a list, (), a hash ref, a code ref, `wantarray ? LIST : REF`, `&$c()`, `$c->()`, `\@a`, `scalar(f())`, the statement modifier, map / grep (right already: another reader), bare arrays, `for ($aref)`, `reverse` / `sort` of a call) + for2.pl (12: element / hash-element refs, substr alias, a tied scalar's FETCH count, blessed, values, slices, `\(@a)`, do, ternary): perl = tree on all; base wrong on 13.  The perf-levers foreach rows all pass (bare arrays keep their arms; the emission is byte-identical).
GUARD: Pl/t/transpile-test-11.t row 12, inverse FAILS on the base.  ir-spec §6.2, DECIDED ## s543e.


=== CLOSED at MAIN-READY-104 `8959afae` (the reviewing session, 2026-11-21; s543e): the suspect in this task (#267`s vector rule) was NOT the cause: the foreach flattener iterated any box`s referent; a box is now one element.  Emission unchanged.  Review probe (5 lines: calls returning one array ref / hash ref / a list / nothing / two refs, method calls, code-ref calls, `for (\@a)`, `for ($r)`, the bare-array fast arms, the modifier form): tree = perl, main wrong on 3.
subject: SILENT WRONG: a foreach list containing a SUB CALL that returns a reference is FLATTENED -- `for (mk()) { ref $_ }` with `sub mk { [1,2] }` iterates the referent's elements
triage_reason: a foreach list holding a sub call that returns a reference is flattened -- ordinary code, first candidate
